verdict.rationale: Anytype's docs describe a maintained Docker image for self-hosting the sync/backup network and a local-only mode that removes reliance on Anytype's own backend, letting users run the core sync infrastructure themselves (anytype-docs-19, anytype-docs-6, anytype-docs-23, anytype-docs-39, anytype-docs-30). This is first-party documentation only; there is no independent/hands-on report confirming a full self-hosted deployment works end-to-end, and the app itself (desktop/mobile clients) is not open-source under an OSI license per community comment (anytype-comm-12), raising some openness caveats. missing for 10: independent verification of self-hosted docker deployment, clarity on whether the full stack (not just the backup node) can be self-hosted, and resolution of the source-available licensing critique.
